newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher despite BoF inaction.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher despite BoF inaction.

text.p: French stocks closed at a record high on Thursday and the market remained in a bullish mood despite the Bank of France's inaction on interest rates.
The market was supported by gains on Wall Street, a strong dollar and rising debt markets in France, dealers said.
Many dealers expected the Bank to cut its intervention rate after its policy-setting meeting earlier. Shares dipped from their highs when the Bank declined to cut rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 19.79 points or 0.83 percent at 2,407.77. The CAC-40 futures contract was down two points at 2,408.
"It's a true rising market with lots of volume. There are no sellers," said one trader who predicted the market would continue to rise.
Another said that shares, though disappointed at the lack of a rate cut on Thursday, dealers expected cuts to come relatively soon.
"Sentiment is positive, there is an increase in liquidity that is not slowing," another trader said.

Pinault-Printemps Redoute closed up 6.05 percent at 2,278 francs. Most traders cited no specific reason, but some said the stock is among cheapest in retail sector on a price to earnings ratio basis. One trader said a favourable article in weekly magazine Vie Francaise helped lift the share.
Cap Gemini closed 4.79 percent higher at 269 francs on resurgence of rumours that the Debis SH unit of Germany's Daimler would increase its stake in the French computer company.
The rumour holds that Debis would offer 300 francs per share to increase its stake from 24.4 percent to about 50 percent.
Cap Gemini declined to comment on the rumour and Debis said it had no plans to raise its stake in Cap Gemini.
Havas closed up 3.03 percent at 400.80 francs after newspapers reported it would announce bid to buy out CEP minority shareholders later today. CEP shares were suspended.
Havas declined to comment on the rumours. Industry sources told Reuters that Havas and CEP would both hold board meetings this afternoon on the bid.
Axa was up 1.64 percent to 347.50 francs, as the value rebounds after falling on Wednesday on fears of dilution from share issuance as part of an early conversion of outstanding convertible bonds.
